request: Compare openings and continuous Earth routes for illuminated-land/water balance, weak unlit regions and long water-dominated stretches at saved2–3×, probably2×; provide selectable presets and pros/cons.

implementation.changed: Four researched angle presets and descriptions replace the earlier opening-only suggestions; current production opening remains as fifth reference. Shared helper explains2×/3×, presets retain chosen speed. Speed field formats15 significant digits to suppress floating-point display debris such as3.0000000000000004; state/export keep their full numeric rate.
implementation.unchanged: 8K asset, production120/25/22.5 opening,0.003rad/s default, full continuous rotation, renderer, sky/camera behavior, storage/network behavior and held optimization candidates.
implementation.adoption: No candidate is final owner approval. Settings remain temporary until user shares a choice.

comparison.search: 120 coarse and150 refined latitude/roll candidates with longitude phase search;23 fine finalists. This is a bounded search, not proof of a global optimum.

methods.nightTexture: 8K production JPEG filtered to2K in memory for sparse CPU sampling
methods.dayTexture: 8K historical day JPEG filtered to2K, qualitative blue-water proxy only
methods.waterProxy: Day blue>red×1.18+5 && blue>green×1.03 && red<105. Clouds, haze, shallow water and green terrain are misclassified. NOT a geographic land/ocean mask.
methods.score: Light coverage ×(.35+.65×distributed15tileFraction). Fullcycle and first3/5min ranked separately; opening phase has extra weight.
methods.lowLightThreshold: <1% warm coverage; not a calibrated human dimness threshold
methods.sourceOrientation: Current orientNightEarth(THREE,earth,camera,opening) direct call; longitude phase can vary opening but not complete-loop statistics.

limitations: CPU proxies require rendered review and do not establish visual quality. Previously favored proxies disappointed the owner.
Actual spacecraft occlusion, tone mapping, night material shading, atmosphere, hover, drag and room movement are omitted. Fixed overview crop only.
Blue day-image threshold is not a reliable unlit-land classifier. We do not claim true land/water percentages or exact unlit-land durations.
At3× the same path takes2/3 the listed2×times. Speed cannot remove ocean or empty geography, only change its duration.
Art selection only; no runtime performance, memory, heat or battery measurements or benefits.

findings.recommendation: Coastal Asia at2× is the best overall compromise of the tested routes, not a solution to constant illumination. Tilted Asia is the more cinematic alternative.
findings.coastal: Recognizable coastline/island/water separation in the full scene and strongest complete-cycle warm-light proxy of the four. Attractive first minute, but inland dimness around1–3min and later multi-minute darkness remain.
findings.tilted: Broader initial lit sweep and sculptural coastline around2–3min. Roll135 prioritizes art over familiar orientation. Less average light than Coastal, dimmer patches within first minute, a major weak interval approximately4:25–9:10on wide at2×.
findings.corridor: Highest first3minute mean light of the four across layouts; still not continuously bright. Resembles the previously rejected coastal opening, and has the worst full-loop low-light streak (up to~6:56at2×in the proxy).
findings.american: Strongest immediate lit-city spectacle. Fades rapidly across western terrain then Pacific; approximately2:05–6:18wide weak interval at2×. Longest fullcycle low-light proxy nearly tied with Coastal; timing of that interval is worse for early visitors.
findings.rejected: Extra US tilts, Europe/India openings and additional artistic phases retained in raw comparisons. Many looked good briefly but dimmed quickly; high-latitude views replace ocean with sparsely lit terrain.
findings.limit: No tested orientation keeps a full revolution lit. Several-minute weak intervals remain for every finalist. Eliminating them would require a separately approved change such as a bounded back-and-forth path or altered artwork, not another angle alone.
